To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a new way to control the frequency of a laser by controlling the pressure in the laser medium.
the frequency of the He– Ne/CH4 ring-laser power resonances can be stabilized with a relative frequency shift of about 10−12 and a reproducibility of about 10 −13.

we have demonstrated that the He-Ne ring laser with the methane absorption cell has a narrow power resonance at the center of a strong absorption line, which has a Lorentz-type line shape, and that the frequency of the He-Ne laser is stabilized by this resonance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of the ring laser parameters on the power resonances and on the reproducibility and accuracy of the laser frequency.
the development of an experimental method of measuring the parameters of power resonances, the study of these resonances, and the stabilization of the ring laser frequency.
the study of the properties of a ring He–Ne/ CH4 laser with a single absorption cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a ring He–Ne laser with a methane cell is a promising frequency standard for the red spectral region.

the He-Ne/ CH4 ring laser is a very useful and practical device for frequency stabilization of the He-Ne laser, and that the ring laser can be used as an effective frequency reference for the He-Ne line at λ=3.39 μm.
the He–Ne ring CH4 laser can operate with high stability and with reproducible frequencies in the presence of narrow power resonant lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the He–Ne ring lasers with the methane absorption cell can be used as a frequency reference with a frequency reproducibility of 1 part in 10 ^{12}.
the He-Ne/Ch4 ring laser is a very useful tool for spectroscopic studies.
the He–Ne laser with a methane absorption line is a convenient tool for the study of the power resonant phenomena.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency shifts of narrow power resonaces can be reduced by an order of magnitude compared to those in a conventional He–Ne/He laser.
the frequency of the He– Ne/CH4 laser is stable and reproducible.

the frequency shifts of power resonances depend on the pressure of the passive medium and on the phase of the coupling, and that the frequency stability of the He–NE/CH4 laser is determined by the stability of the power resonant frequency.
